question: Can we remove this support account's standing administrator access without breaking its approved work?
scope: Acme Support · account usr-042 · tenant acme-support · own queue q-7

alternatives.title: Keep Administrator
alternatives.tradeoff: Preserves current workflows but leaves broad privileges. Interim exposure needs an accountable decision.

alternatives.title: Remove all reporting
alternatives.tradeoff: Narrows access, but interrupts a reporting need the owner has confirmed.

challenge.title: What if the quiet log misses rare work?
challenge.body: Ninety days without admin activity does not rule out a recovery task that happens once a year.
challenge.check: Ask the owner whether any recovery workflow needs administration, and how that access should be handled.

stages.label: Try an unresolved identity

advice.title: Resolve the account before changing access.
advice.reason: This alternative cannot join the account to its custodian. The earlier required-work statement may concern a different person.
advice.condition: Confirm the immutable account mapping and accountable owner. No permission change is supported by a name match.
advice.next: Identity owner: reconcile usr-042 with the authoritative people record.
advice.support: The failed identity join changes whose work the sources can establish.

stages.change: The revised identity source removes the immutable join. The original named-person attribution is no longer supported.

stages.label: Try a failed daily-role test

advice.title: Fix the daily role before rollout.
advice.reason: The export test fails after inherited admin is removed. Recovery access works in its rehearsal, but it cannot replace required everyday reporting.
advice.condition: Revise and retest effective permissions, including denied cross-queue exports. Approval is still required.
advice.next: Alex and Maya: correct the daily role and repeat the required-work checks.
advice.support: The failed required-work check rules out the current candidate. A successful recovery test cannot outweigh it.

stages.change: The daily-role test contradicts the catalogue’s claimed fit. The recovery result is retained for its separate task.

stages.label: Add the successful daily-role test

advice.title: Propose the narrower role and recovery path.
advice.reason: The daily-role test preserves tickets and scoped exports. The separate rehearsal supports temporary annual recovery without standing Administrator.
advice.condition: The designated approver must authorise the production change. Remove the inherited grant and verify the resulting production permissions and work.
advice.next: Maya and platform approver: review the tested plan for usr-042.
advice.support: Two scoped tests support different required tasks. Neither is production execution or approval.

stages.change: TEST-042-P now supplies daily-work and export-boundary checks. Production implementation remains unobserved.

stages.label: Add permission change and outcome checks

advice.title: The scoped change is observed. Retain the record.
advice.reason: The later record supplies attributed approval, removal of inherited admin, and successful production checks for this account’s daily work.
advice.condition: This does not generalise to other accounts. Reassess changed permissions or required work; production annual recovery remains unobserved.
advice.next: Maya: retain the checks and review the annual recovery arrangement when due.
advice.support: The outcome record is separate from recording a simulated next step. This demo did not make the change.

stages.change: OUT-042 adds later attributed authorization, observed implementation and scoped daily-work results. It is not created by the simulated-choice button.

stages.label: Try irrelevant meeting context

advice.title: Test a role that fits the work.
advice.reason: Keep tickets and own-queue exports. Remove broad administration after the owner reviews the role and its permissions are tested.
advice.condition: Owner review and a controlled permissions check are still needed.
advice.next: Review and test the proposed support role
advice.support: The catalogue supports the role. Its effective permissions are untested.

stages.change: Only the meeting room changed. The recommendation and its unresolved conditions remain the same.

advice.title: Test a role that fits the work.
advice.reason: Keep tickets and own-queue exports. Remove broad administration after the owner reviews the role and its permissions are tested.
advice.condition: Owner review and a controlled permissions check are still needed.
advice.next: Review and test the proposed support role
advice.support: The catalogue supports the role. Its effective permissions are untested.

stages.label: Annual task added

advice.title: Resolve the recovery path first.
advice.reason: The everyday role covers tickets and reporting on paper. Annual recovery needs an additional capability that the quiet activity log missed.
advice.condition: Establish a supported recovery path before removing the access it needs. Owner approval and daily-role testing remain open.
advice.next: Review a recovery path with the owner
advice.support: The annual task is now in scope. No working way to provide temporary recovery access has been demonstrated.

stages.change: Annual recovery falls outside the activity window. A narrower daily role alone no longer covers the confirmed work.

stages.label: Tested recovery path

advice.title: Daily access, with a recovery path.
advice.reason: Use a narrower everyday role, plus tested temporary access for annual recovery. The rehearsal supports the extra capability when the work needs it.
advice.condition: The owner must approve the change, and the everyday role still needs a permissions test. The recovery rehearsal covers one staging environment.
advice.next: Review the combined plan and test the daily role
advice.support: The recovery task, time limit and export boundary passed in this fictional rehearsal. That strengthens this option; it does not establish production readiness or a calibrated confidence score.

stages.change: A controlled rehearsal demonstrates temporary recovery access. The combined option is now supported within that test’s scope.

stages.label: Runbook only

advice.title: Prove the recovery path works.
advice.reason: The runbook describes a useful option, but does not show that recovery, expiry or export limits work. Keep that gap visible before choosing the combined plan.
advice.condition: A controlled recovery rehearsal, daily-role test and owner approval are still needed. No access change is authorized.
advice.next: Ask for a controlled recovery rehearsal
advice.support: The process is documented. Its implementation and effective permissions remain unverified.

stages.change: In this alternative, only a runbook is available. The combined option needs a successful test before we can rely on it.

stages.label: Path unavailable

advice.title: Find another supported recovery path.
advice.reason: The daily role cannot perform recovery, and this environment cannot provide temporary admin access. The proposed combination is not currently feasible.
advice.condition: Establish another recovery method with the owner. Neither removing the capability nor retaining permanent admin is approved here.
advice.support: The prepared platform constraint rules out this path. The sources do not establish a safe replacement.

stages.change: In this alternative, the environment cannot provide temporary access. This recovery path is ruled out.

activity@activity / r1.label: App activity
activity@activity / r1.claim: Daily activity does not establish all required work.
activity@activity / r1.quote: For usr-042, the selected 90-day window shows tickets and own-queue exports, with no administration events. Ingestion coverage is 97%; three days are missing.
activity@activity / r1.why: Supports investigating narrower daily access. The window cannot cover annual recovery.
activity@activity / r1.limit: Missing days and infrequent work rule out treating absence as proof of no need.

recovery-tested@recovery-rehearsal / r1.label: Recovery rehearsal
recovery-tested@recovery-rehearsal / r1.claim: Temporary recovery access worked in a controlled test.
recovery-tested@recovery-rehearsal / r1.quote: Fictional test record: In Acme support staging, Alex received an approved 45-minute administrative grant, completed the annual queue-recovery task, and could export only the support team's own queue. Cross-queue export attempts were denied. The grant expired and a subsequent admin action was denied. The record includes test approval, grant, task, expiry and denial logs; Maya reviewed the result.
recovery-tested@recovery-rehearsal / r1.why: Provides a demonstrated recovery path alongside narrower everyday access in this prepared example. The expiry and export checks are observed results, not promises in a runbook.
recovery-tested@recovery-rehearsal / r1.limit: One synthetic tenant and rehearsal on 29 September. No claim about a vendor's real capabilities. The everyday role still needs its own effective-permission test. Test approval is not approval to change anyone's access.

daily-test@daily-test / r1-failed.why: The candidate role fails confirmed daily work even though the separate recovery rehearsal succeeded.
daily-test@daily-test / r1-failed.limit: Passing recovery is not proof that the daily role fits. No production change or approval is supplied.

sourceFamilies.question: What finding or review actually needs a decision?
sourceFamilies.limit: Workflow status is not verified treatment or approval.

sourceFamilies.question: Which immutable account belongs to which custodian?
sourceFamilies.limit: Names and employment do not establish permissions.

sourceFamilies.question: What can the exact account or service do, including inherited grants?
sourceFamilies.limit: A role catalogue is not a test of effective rights.

sourceFamilies.question: What happened in the observed window and what coverage is missing?
sourceFamilies.limit: No observed event is not proof of no activity or no need.

sourceFamilies.question: Which change produced which artifact?
sourceFamilies.limit: A merge or component match is not production treatment.
sourceFamilies.coverage: Not used: no software artifact treatment in this account review.

sourceFamilies.question: What ran, and what exact outcome was independently checked?
sourceFamilies.limit: Implementation does not establish effective treatment or authority.

sourceFamilies.question: What requirement, boundary, approval and validity apply?
sourceFamilies.limit: A request or runbook does not implement or authorise a safeguard.

sourceFamilies.question: Who owns the treatment and which dependencies remain?
sourceFamilies.limit: A done ticket does not prove verification or delivery authority.

sourceFamilies.question: Which earlier incident or review makes a check relevant?
sourceFamilies.limit: Past similarity does not predict the new outcome.

sourceFamilies.question: Which attributed work or delivery constraint affects the choice?
sourceFamilies.limit: A date or statement does not grant approval or make an obligation mandatory.
